 Rainy season: Avoid swimming, water activities and unnecessary risks for temporary thrills 
 Aida Aziz

 By Aida Aziz
 IPOH: The public is advised to avoid water-based activities, including swimming in rivers and waterfalls, during the rainy season, particularly the ongoing northeast monsoon.
 The Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) said four incidents involving drowning and missing persons swept away by currents had been recorded in the state as of November 12 this year.
 It said the northeast monsoon increases the risk of water surges, strong currents and flash floods, particularly in rivers, waterfalls and water-based recreational areas.
 “One drowning incident occurred on November 8 at Air Terjun Taman Suria in Taiping, followed by another on November 9 at Sungai Pinang Besar, Pulau Pangkor.
 “Further incidents were reported on November 10 at Sungai Jahang in Gopeng and on November 11 at Sungai Jalong.
 “Of the four incidents, three victims were reported dead, while one case involved a person feared drowned,” it said in a statement.
 In view of the incidents, JBPM Perak advised the public to stay away from rivers with strong currents.
 The public was also urged to comply with instructions from the authorities and warning signboards, as well as keep a close watch on children near water bodies.
 Water-based recreational activities should be stopped whenever weather conditions become unfavourable.
 “Do not put yourself at risk for temporary enjoyment. The safety of yourself and your family must always come first,” it added.
 Aida Aziz
